true_answer: Often we are interested in the element(s) whose image is a particular element y of in the codomain. The notation above works: f − 1 ({ y }) is the set of all elements in the domain that f sends to y . It makes sense to think of this as a set: there might not be anything sent to y (if y is not in the range), in which case f − 1 ({ y }) | ∅ . Or f might send multiple elements to y (if f is not injective). As a notational convenience, we usually drop the set braces around the y and write f inf ( y ) instead for this set. WARNING: f − 1 ( y ) is not an inverse function!
